subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB330 LANDED (wave 56). RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.27.3 'An OPEN statement that specifies file-name-1 more than once shall not be specified in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement' -> OK 14.9.27.3 3)). DETERMINATION (the standard's own words settle it, no owner question): 'file-name-1' is the FORMAT TERM the ellipsis repeats, and the statement's general rule 14.9.27.4 GR20 (cite.py --find -> 14.9.27.4 20)) names that form 'If more than one file-name is specified in an OPEN statement'; the family (CLOSE 14.9.6.3 SR3, DELETE FILE 14.9.10.3 SR4, INITIATE, TERMINATE, VALIDATE) bans the multi-operand statement. COBOL1616 now fires when the statement's file-names, summed over every open-mode group, number more than one; a duplicate is one case of that. MEASURED (w56a/probe/ecp1.cob): BEFORE `OPEN OUTPUT F1 F2` in imp-1 compiled clean while `CLOSE F1 F2` drew 1612; AFTER both rejected. Region A only: a multi-file OPEN in a WHEN body compiles (positive golden + SingleOperandInImp1_MultiInWhenBody_Accepted). 2023 only: the exception-checking PERFORM is a COBOL-2023 introduction (COBOL0900 below).
